rules.title: Map comprehension expression
rules.statement: `{ KEY : VALUE for NAME in ITER [if GUARD] }` is a map-comprehension expression: KEY, VALUE, ITER, GUARD are arbitrary exprs, NAME a single bound identifier; GUARD is optional.
examples: { k: v*2 for k in items if v > 0 }

rules.title: Writ literal @ sigil is outermost-only
rules.statement: A Writ (SDN) literal is introduced by a leading `@` sigil (`@{...}`, `@[...]`, `@"s"`, `@42`, `@true`, `@null`, ...); only the outermost literal of a nested structure requires the sigil — inner map/array values (writ_val) parse as plain `{...}`/`[...]` and accept but do not require a redundant `@` prefix.

rules.title: Typed dense-array Writ literal
rules.statement: `@<ElemType>[v1, v2, ...]` is a typed dense-array Writ literal (WRIT_TYPED_ARRAY) carrying the element TYPE and an ITEMS list of writ_val; trailing comma allowed; may be empty.

rules.title: Typed map Writ literal
rules.statement: `@<K,V>{...}` (key+value type) or `@<K>{...}` (key type only) is a typed-map Writ literal (WRIT_TYPED_MAP) with TYPE (and optional RET_TYPE) plus an ITEMS list of writ_entry; trailing comma allowed; may be empty.

rules.title: Writ list-comprehension literal
rules.statement: `@[ VALUE for NAME in ITER [if GUARD] ]` is a Writ list-comprehension literal (WRIT_LIST_COMP); GUARD is optional.

rules.title: Writ map-comprehension literal
rules.statement: `@{ KEY : VALUE for NAME in ITER [if GUARD] }` is a Writ map-comprehension literal (WRIT_MAP_COMP); GUARD is optional.

rules.title: Writ scalar literal forms
rules.statement: Top-level writ_lit alternatives, tried in order: list-comp, map-comp, typed-map, typed-array, plain map `@{...}`, plain array `@[...]`, `@` raw-string, `@` string (WRIT_STR), `@` float (WRIT_FLOAT), `@-`INTEGER (WRIT_NEG_INT), `@`INTEGER (WRIT_INT), `@true`/`@false` (WRIT_BOOL), `@null` (WRIT_NULL).

rules.title: Writ map-entry key forms
rules.statement: A writ_entry key is a quoted STRING, a plain INTEGER, or a negative INTEGER (`-`INTEGER, flagged LO_NEG) to support TinyObjectMap-style integer-keyed maps; value is a writ_val.

rules.title: Writ runtime-capture placeholders
rules.statement: Inside a writ_val, `$IDENT` (WRIT_CAP_IDENT) and `${expr}` (WRIT_CAP_EXPR) splice a runtime value into the otherwise-literal Writ structure at construction time.

rules.title: Embedded Type literal in Writ value
rules.statement: `<type:IDENT path_step*>` (CFG_SLOT_TYPE) embeds a type path with an IDENT-only head plus additional path segments, used for CFG.path slot extraction; `<type:simple_type>` (WRIT_TYPE_LIT) is the general form accepting any simple_type so generic instantiations (e.g. `Vec<u8>`, `Result<T,E>`) reach sema as a structured TYPE child. Both embed a Logos Type as a first-class Writ value.

rules.title: Array literal
rules.statement: `[e1, e2, ...]` is an array literal (ARR_LIT) with an ITEMS list of expr; trailing comma allowed; may be empty (`[]`).

rules.title: Tuple literal requires a comma
rules.statement: `(e1, e2, ...)` with 2+ comma-separated exprs, or `(e,)` with exactly one expr followed by a mandatory trailing comma, is a tuple literal (TUPLE_LIT); the trailing comma in the single-element form disambiguates the 1-tuple from a parenthesized expression.

rules.title: Closure parameter type may be omitted
rules.statement: A closure_param's `: Type` annotation is optional (`|x|` vs `|x: T|`); when omitted, the parameter's type is inferred from the surrounding `fn(T) -> R` formal at the call site (sema), not fixed by the grammar.
rules.uncertainty: The inference mechanism itself is implemented in sema, outside this slice; only the grammar's relaxed-annotation shape is directly evidenced here.

rules.title: Closure parameter binding forms
rules.statement: closure_param accepts: `&mut IDENT` (ref+mut, no type), `&IDENT` (ref, no type), `ref IDENT: Type`, `mut IDENT: Type`, `mut IDENT` (no type), `(pat_binding_list): Type` (tuple-destructuring param, type mandatory), `IDENT: Type`, or bare `IDENT` (no type).

rules.title: Closure expression forms
rules.statement: closure_expr = [`move`] (`||` | `|` closure_param_list? `|`) [`-> RetType`] BODY, where BODY is either a block `{ ... }` or a bare expression; the expression-body alternatives are tried after the block-body alternatives so `|x| { ... }` still parses with a block body rather than a struct-literal/block expression.

rules.title: Parenthesized expression
rules.statement: `(expr)` is a parenthesized expression (PAREN_EXPR) wrapping a single expr; distinct from tuple_lit, which requires a comma.

rules.title: quote_item! typed-AST item literal
rules.statement: `quote_item! { item* }` parses zero or more item declarations as its body and produces a QUOTE_ITEM node; sema deep-clones the parsed items into a fresh Writ module, serializes it, and emits a byte-slice (WritStatic) literal value.

rules.title: quote_expr! typed-AST expression literal
rules.statement: `quote_expr! { expr }` parses a single expression as its body and produces a QUOTE_EXPR node; sema deep-clones the expr's AnyVal as the root TOM of a fresh Writ doc (root schema_type_code set from CODE) and emits an ExprBlob value, spliced via metacall.

rules.title: quote_ty! typed Type literal
rules.statement: `quote_ty! { type_ref }` parses a single type expression as its body and produces a QUOTE_TY node; sema resolves it to a TypeRef and emits the same `Type{kind, name, size}` struct literal that `type_of::<T>()` produces.

rules.title: Generic type-parameter list
rules.statement: `<type_param, ...>` is a generic parameter list; the same production also serves as a specialization-pattern argument list (e.g. `<i32>`, `<*T>`, `<[T;4]>`) — the grammar does not distinguish a type-var parameter from a concrete specialization arg; that classification is done in sema.

rules.title: HRTB binder is parsed and semantically discarded
rules.statement: `for<'a, 'b, ...> Trait<...>` (HRTB) is accepted as a bound prefix on every trait_bound alternative, but Logos does not track lifetimes structurally: the binder is parsed into a disposable head and dropped, so `for<'a> Fn(&'a T)` is semantically identical to `Fn(&T)`.
rules.divergence: Rust's HRTB binder affects variance/soundness checking; Logos parses the syntax for source compatibility but erases it semantically (no lifetime-parametric trait-bound checking) — no existing DIVERGENCES.md tag covers this; noted here as a one-line divergence.

rules.title: Relaxed bound syntax `?IDENT`
rules.statement: `? IDENT` is grammatically accepted as a relaxed trait_bound (TRAIT_BOUND with RELAXED=true) for any IDENT, opting out of an implicit bound on the type parameter (intended use: `?Sized`).
rules.uncertainty: The comment at this site states sema rejects any name other than `Sized`; that rejection is not itself visible in this slice.

rules.title: Fn-family parenthesized trait-bound sugar
rules.statement: `IDENT(T1, T2, ...) [-> R]` and `IDENT() [-> R]` are parenthesized trait-bound forms (e.g. `Fn(T)->R`, `FnMut(T)`, `FnOnce()`); the argument types populate PARAMS (parallel to the angle-bracket TYPE_PARAMS slot) and an optional `-> R` populates RET_TYPE. Available both with and without a leading HRTB binder.

rules.title: Lifetime parameter with outlives bound
rules.statement: A lifetime_param is `'a : 'b (+ 'c)*` (with an outlives bound list of one or more lifetimes) or bare `'a`; each outlives lifetime is wrapped in a LIFETIME_PARAM sub-node so it is collected by the parent's `$...` array (bare LIFETIME tokens are not).

rules.title: Parameter-pack repeat-group type param
rules.statement: `#(type_param), *` is a REPEAT_GROUP type_param form wrapping an inner type_param with a repetition marker (OP=1).
rules.uncertainty: Surface syntax and exact repetition semantics are inferred from this single grammar line; no worked example is visible in this slice.

rules.title: Type parameter with lifetime-outlives bound
rules.statement: `IDENT : lifetime_param (+ lifetime_param)*` is a type_param form (TYPE_PARAM) whose ITEMS are all LIFETIME_PARAM nodes, distinguished from the ordinary trait-bound TYPE_PARAM form (whose ITEMS are TRAIT_BOUND nodes) by the element code; must be tried before the trait-bound alternative so the leading `'` resolves the choice.

rules.title: Const generic parameter forms
rules.statement: type_param accepts `const IDENT ... : Type` (variadic const param, IS_VARIADIC=true), `const # IDENT : Type` (const param bound to a name-variable, NAME_VAR), and `const IDENT : Type` (fixed-name const param) — all produce CONST_PARAM.

rules.title: Variadic type parameter (pack)
rules.statement: `IDENT ... : trait_bound (+ trait_bound)*` and bare `IDENT ...` are variadic type_param forms (TYPE_PARAM, IS_VARIADIC=true), with or without trait bounds respectively.

rules.title: Name-variable type parameter
rules.statement: `# IDENT : trait_bound (+ trait_bound)*` and bare `# IDENT` are type_param forms bound to a name-variable (NAME_VAR) rather than a fixed identifier, with or without trait bounds respectively — a metaprogramming-facing parameter-naming mechanism.
rules.uncertainty: The consuming mechanism (how NAME_VAR is bound at instantiation) lives outside this slice; only the grammar shape is evidenced here.

rules.title: Type parameter with default type
rules.statement: `IDENT : trait_bound (+ trait_bound)* = Type` and `IDENT = Type` supply a default TYPE on a type_param, with or without trait bounds respectively.

rules.title: Generic instantiation type-argument list
rules.statement: `<type_or_lt_arg, ...>` (type_arg_list) is a comma-separated list of type or lifetime arguments used for generic instantiation in type position (e.g. `Vec<i32>`); trailing comma allowed.

rules.title: Package-qualified free-function call
rules.statement: `IDENT ('.' IDENT)+ '::' IDENT (args)` — a dotted package-path prefix (RECEIVER = first segment, QUAL_PARTS = the remaining `.`-segments) followed by `::IDENT(...)` — calls the free function whose `.package` equals the joined dotted path; this disambiguates same-named free functions across packages (e.g. `logos.lang.mem::replace` vs `logos.lang.ptr::replace`). A turbofish variant `... '::' IDENT '::' <T>(args)` supplies explicit type args (GENERIC_CALL). Tried before the single-IDENT `::` call forms since the mandatory `.`-segment makes it unambiguous.

rules.title: Turbofish on type vs. turbofish on method
rules.statement: `Type::<T>::method(args)` (STATIC_CALL, turbofish on the type's own generics) is grammatically distinct from `Type::method::<T>(args)` (STATIC_CALL, turbofish on the method's own generics, TYPE_PARAMS applied to the associated fn); the method-turbofish alternative is tried before the plain `Type::method(args)` form to resolve the ambiguity.

rules.title: UFCS qualified-path call resolves by concrete type only
rules.statement: `<Type as Trait>::method(args)` is accepted as a STATIC_CALL keyed on RECEIVER=Type and NAME=method; the `as Trait` qualifier is parsed but consumed/dropped, so dispatch resolves purely from the concrete type — the trait qualifier does not participate in overload disambiguation.
rules.divergence: In Rust, the `<Type as Trait>::method` qualifier disambiguates among multiple trait impls providing a same-named method; here it is grammar-accepted but discarded, relying solely on type-based method resolution (see also the already-blessed trait-qualified-UFCS entry in docs/DIVERGENCES.md "Trait::method(recv, ...)" dispatch-on-first-arg).

rules.title: Call through a name-variable callee
rules.statement: `# IDENT (args)` and `# (expr) (args)` call through a metaprogramming name-variable callee (CALL, NAME_VAR); the second form allows the name-variable itself to be an arbitrary parenthesized expr.
rules.uncertainty: The binding/resolution of NAME_VAR callees is implemented outside this slice; only the call-site grammar shape is evidenced here.

rules.title: `::new` static-call sugar with turbofish
rules.statement: `IDENT::<T>::new(args)` is accepted as a STATIC_CALL with NAME bound to the `new` keyword, alongside the general `IDENT::<T>::method(args)` form; `IDENT::new(args)` (no turbofish) is likewise a STATIC_CALL alongside the general `IDENT::IDENT(args)` form.

rules.title: Plain call expression
rules.statement: `IDENT(args)`, `new(args)`, and `null(args)` are plain CALL expressions with an optional comma-separated, optionally trailing-comma-terminated call_arg_list.

rules.title: Associated-type equality clause in bound args
rules.statement: Inside a trait bound's `<...>` argument list, each bound_arg is either a positional type_or_lt_arg or an associated-type equality clause `Name = Type` (ASSOC_EQ_BIND: NAME=assoc-type name, TYPE=rhs type AST); the two forms may be mixed in one comma-separated list (e.g. `Iterator<Item = T>`-style constraints).
